description: Composite of four property plots: (a)-(d) are experimental-versus-simulated flow stress-strain curves at four deformation temperatures. Every panel has the x-axis "True strain" (0-0.8, ticks every 0.1) and the y-axis "Stress (MPa)", with different y-ranges: (a) 70-245, (b) 60-210, (c) 25-150, (d) 20-120 MPa. An in-panel legend defines two line styles — solid "Experimental" and dashed open-circle "Simulated" — plus four colour-coded deformation conditions: 0.01 s⁻¹ (green), 0.1 s⁻¹ (magenta), 1 s⁻¹ (blue), 10 s⁻¹ (red). Flow stress falls monotonically with rising temperature and rises with strain rate: in (a) the 10 s⁻¹ curve climbs above the 210 MPa gridline while 0.01 s⁻¹ plateaus just above the 105 MPa gridline; in (d) the corresponding pair spans the space below the 120 MPa gridline. At 1050 °C and 1150 °C the low-strain-rate curves show a stress peak followed by pronounced softening (DRX-type), whereas at 850 °C all four curves rise continuously with only a late plateau. Dashed simulated curves closely track the solid experimental curves in all four panels. The figure demonstrates that the constitutive model reproduces measured flow behaviour over the whole temperature-strain-rate window.

subfigures.description: Flow stress-strain curves at 850 °C, y-axis Stress (MPa) 70-245, x-axis True strain 0-0.8. Four conditions 850°C_0.01s⁻¹ (green), 850°C_0.1s⁻¹ (magenta), 850°C_1s⁻¹ (blue), 850°C_10s⁻¹ (red), each with an Experimental solid line and a Simulated dashed open-circle line. All curves rise monotonically; the 10 s⁻¹ curve ends above the 210 MPa gridline.

Curves at 950 °C, Stress 60-210 MPa. Curves 950°C_0.01s⁻¹ (green), 950°C_0.1s⁻¹ (magenta), 950°C_1s⁻¹ (blue), 950°C_10s⁻¹ (red). The green and magenta curves show a peak near strain 0.2-0.3 followed by mild softening; blue and red rise and level off, red reaching about the 205-210 MPa band.

Curves at 1050 °C, Stress 25-150 MPa. 1050°C_0.01s⁻¹ (green) and 1050°C_0.1s⁻¹ (magenta) peak around 50-75 MPa and then soften clearly; 1050°C_1s⁻¹ (blue) rises to just above the 100 MPa gridline then dips and rises again; 1050°C_10s⁻¹ (red) rises past the 150 MPa gridline.

Curves at 1150 °C, Stress 20-120 MPa — the lowest stress level of the group. 1150°C_0.01s⁻¹ (green) peaks between the 40 and 60 MPa gridlines then softens; 1150°C_0.1s⁻¹ (magenta) peaks near the 60-70 MPa level and declines; 1150°C_1s⁻¹ (blue) peaks near the 80-90 MPa band; 1150°C_10s⁻¹ (red) rises to just above the 110 MPa gridline. Simulated dashed curves closely follow the experimental ones.

observations.observation: The figure is a four-panel composite (a)-(d), each panel a plot of Stress (MPa) versus True strain over 0-0.8 with tick labels 0.1 to 0.8.
Each panel legend distinguishes a solid line labelled 'Experimental' from a dashed line with open circles labelled 'Simulated'.
Four deformation conditions are colour-coded in every panel: 0.01 s⁻¹ (green), 0.1 s⁻¹ (magenta), 1 s⁻¹ (blue) and 10 s⁻¹ (red).
The y-axis range differs per panel: (a) 70-245 MPa, (b) 60-210 MPa, (c) 25-150 MPa, (d) 20-120 MPa.
In panel (a) (850 °C) all four curves increase monotonically with strain; the 10 s⁻¹ curve ends above the 210 MPa gridline while the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve plateaus just above the 105 MPa gridline.

In panels (c) and (d) the low strain-rate curves (0.01 s⁻¹ and 0.1 s⁻¹) show a clear stress peak followed by softening, and this softening becomes more pronounced as temperature rises from 1050 to 1150 °C.

The highest curve of each panel decreases with temperature: above the 210 MPa gridline in (a), near the 205-210 MPa band in (b), above the 150 MPa gridline in (c), and just above the 110 MPa gridline in (d).
Within each panel the flow stress increases with strain rate, the 10 s⁻¹ curve always lying highest and the 0.01 s⁻¹ curve lowest.
The caption states that panel (a) is 850 °C, (b) 950 °C, (c) 1050 °C and (d) 1150 °C, i.e. the flow stress-strain curves at different deformation temperatures.
The caption states each panel compares experimental and simulated curves; the pixels confirm that the dashed simulated curves closely follow the solid experimental curves in all four panels.

The citing text reports that errors between predicted and experimental curves occur at 10 s⁻¹, where high strain rate hinders DRX nucleation and growth so that work hardening dominates and no obvious stress softening appears in the initial stage.

The citing text attributes the model validation metrics to Table 2, not to this figure: correlation coefficients exceeding 0.99 under constant deformation conditions and AARE values of 3.91 % and 6.65 %.
